name: permissive-rule-outranks-protection
prompt: fixture_permissive_rule_outranks_protection.py is our 24 V buck board. Is anything wrong with this rule set? Fix whatever is.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components origin/main 9c398d3 (the installed package in the eval venv); the build uses the lc-eval parts chain, the example catalogue then ideal parts, so no parts database is needed. The fixture module is fixture_permissive_rule_outranks_protection.py, Design PermissiveRuleOutranksProtectionDesign; lc_power_board.py imports box from lc_radio_board.py. The fixture's ladder: 0 defaults, 1 VIN width, 2 a 0.6 VIN keep-away to AnyObject, 4 a 0.1 escape clearance on IsTrace & OnLayer(0) to AnyObject. The escape rule's condition matches the VIN trace on L1, so it outranks the keep-away. Measured on the bare fixture (this suite's own run, 2026-11-03): the layer-0 GND pour sat 0.11 from the VIN route (0.1 + 0.01, the spike S9 offset). Narrowing the escape rule to IsTrace & OnLayer(0) & ~InputRail() (this suite's own solution) gave 0.61, no issue. Raising the keep-away above 4 also gives 0.61 but leaves the escape rule matching every L1 trace; the judge asks for narrowing. Deleting the escape rule fails the check. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Add tags and design rules, in the fixture module, fixture_permissive_rule_outranks_protection.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name. Do not add, move or remove parts, nets, routes, vias or pours, and do not set Route.Config on a route; assigning a tag to an existing object is fine. Build the design and read the result back to show the rules applied. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each rule with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A diagnosis that the priority-4 escape clearance matches every L1 trace, VIN included, and so beats the priority-2 keep-away; the escape rule narrowed to the objects it is for while kept at 0.1; and COMPLETION.md with the measured pour gap to the VIN route before and after.

assertions.text: the layer-0 pour sits the 0.6 mm keep-away (plus 0.01) from the VIN route, the VIN route is still 0.5 mm, and the 0.1 mm escape clearance rule is still in the design
the diagnosis names the override: the escape rule's condition matches the VIN trace on L1 and its higher priority beats the keep-away
the fix narrows the escape rule's condition so it no longer matches the VIN trace, rather than only reordering priorities
COMPLETION.md reports the pour gap to the VIN route read from the built design, not build success alone
